newsitem.title: ISRAEL: De Beers diamond sales to Israel up 35 percent.
newsitem.headline: De Beers diamond sales to Israel up 35 percent.

text.p: The De Beers Central Selling Organisation (CSO) increased sales of diamonds to Israel by 35 percent to $1.1 billion in 1996, the group's president, Anthony Oppenheimer, said on Thursday.
"There are always a number of problems but on the whole we have managed to increase our supplies very substantially in 1996 over 1995," he told Reuters.
He said sales continued to rise in 1997 although he did not have figures.
In 1996 Israel's exports of polished and uncut diamonds totalled nearly $5 billion. The CSO directly supplied 30 percent of Israel's rough diamond imports last year.

Israel has been seeking a bigger allotment of diamonds and higher quality stones from the CSO. The London-based organisation sells stones worth more than $4.5 billion a year to a select group of so-called "sight" traders.

Oppenheimer, in Israel for the CSO's twice yearly liaison meeting with government and industry officials, said among the problems discussed were the direct purchase of diamonds from Russia and the allotment of new sight holders.
"A lot of diamonds came as you might say through the back door last year to Israel," Oppenheimer said.
He did not have figures but added: "This year there been much less, as far as I know, hardly significant quantities and at quite high prices."
Oppenheimer said the CSO could not grant Israel new sight holders until the situation with Russia was settled.
De Beers and Russia agreed on a draft trade agreement last October. Russia has said it would decide on April 15 whether to sign the stalled deal.
The CSO accounts for 70-80 percent of the world's diamond supplies. "It fluctuates slightly, depending on whether the Russians sell to us or they don't sell," Oppenheimer said.
